description: Data-only QA scenario manifest for the AlKhayal acceptance runner (scripts/run-acceptance-tests.ps1). Maps scenario IDs to exact xUnit FullyQualifiedName test selectors. This file contains no logic; later batches extend it by adding titles/tests to placeholder entries or appending new scenarios. Never edit an already-mapped scenario's tests without re-executing them.
numberingCaveat: The repository has no committed canonical QA-001..QA-100 checklist. QA-001..QA-017 follow docs/qa/phase-1-coverage.md (QA-004/QA-005 are authoritative; the rest are marked inferred there). Batch 3 (2026-10-26) confirmed the phase/module ranges per the QA owner's explicit instruction and defined QA-018..QA-039; see docs/qa/phase-2-coverage.md. QA-040..QA-100 remain unmapped scaffold placeholders under the scaffoldRanges convention below; a later batch that owns the canonical list must replace or confirm them.

statusSemantics.PASS: Every mapped test for the scenario was executed in this run and passed, and the manifest records no manual/browser/desktop/hardware remainder for the scenario.
statusSemantics.PARTIAL: Every mapped test for the scenario ran and passed, but the scenario carries an unexecuted manual remainder (browser-only native, desktop, or hardware portion). PARTIAL is never converted to PASS; the open remainder is reported in the record's manualRemainder and reason.
statusSemantics.FAIL: One or more mapped tests failed, or a mapped test did not appear in the run results (selector mismatch or discovery failure).
statusSemantics.SKIP: Mapped scenario that was outside the requested run scope and therefore not executed in this run.
statusSemantics.BLOCKED: The scenario could not be executed honestly: unmapped placeholder, no automated test mapping, missing tool (dotnet/node), or a build failure. BLOCKED is never converted to PASS.

phase5.module: sales/returns/printing (QA-072..QA-093), frontend/native (QA-086..QA-093 subset), cross-module (QA-094..QA-100 carries numeric phase 5 because the runner validates phase 1..5)

phases.1: Authentication, bootstrap, users, sessions, settings, features (Batch 1 scope)
phases.2: Catalog, products, units, variants, barcodes + inventory warehouse, receipt/issue, adjustment, transfer, count, FIFO, tracking, ledger projection (QA-018..QA-039 Batch 3 scope)
phases.3: Customers (QA-040..QA-047) and suppliers (QA-048..QA-055); mapped by QA Batch 4 (docs/qa/phase-3-coverage.md), QA-047 remains BLOCKED without an automated mapping
phases.4: Purchases and purchase returns (unmapped placeholder range QA-056..QA-071)
phases.5: Sales, POS, sales returns, printing, frontend shell, native lifecycle (QA-072..QA-093) and cross-module items (QA-094..QA-100, numeric phase 5)

scenarios.notes: Mapped by QA Batch 3 (docs/qa/phase-2-coverage.md).

scenarios.title: Concurrency and projection integrity: two concurrent issues of the last unit admit exactly one and never drive stock negative, and an administrative projection rebuild succeeds, produces an existing verified backup file, records an InventoryAudit projection_rebuild event, and passes VerifyProjectionAsync
scenarios.notes: Mapped by QA Batch 3 (docs/qa/phase-2-coverage.md). The backup file is deleted only inside the test.

scenarios.manualRemainder: Valuation display in WebView2 screens (manual native acceptance; exact integer math itself is automated)

scenarios.notes: Mapped by QA Batch 3 (docs/qa/phase-2-coverage.md).

scenarios.title: FIFO transfer: value moves with origin FIFO order and cost into Basis='transfer' destination layers (one movement row per side for the document), identical transfer replays, an injected destination failure rolls back both sides leaving source layers and no orphan document, the transfer history lists rows with the related warehouse name, and the projection verifies

scenarios.title: Adjustment and count-shortage valuation: negative adjustments and count-recorded shortages consume existing FIFO layers in order (ending value exactly 9600000 at scaled scale-4), discovery of a new positive quantity requires an explicit cost (cost_required), and providing the cost posts exact value (12400000) with RecordedQuantity verification
scenarios.notes: Mapped by QA Batch 3 (docs/qa/phase-2-coverage.md). (Count idempotency is QA-036; adjustment/reconciliation opening-basis legacy path is QA-030.)

scenarios.title: Physical count lifecycle: count draft captures one line per stored variant, posting a different counted quantity posts the exact difference (5→3), posted status and counted values are re-read exactly, an identical count post replays and a changed payload conflicts, stale capture against a moved-on balance version is rejected (stale_count), reversing an already-reversed document is rejected (already_reversed/reversal_conflict), a zero-stock variant can be counted/discovered (BalanceVersion 0) and a count draft can be canceled leaving no movements
scenarios.notes: Mapped by QA Batch 3 (docs/qa/phase-2-coverage.md).

scenarios.title: Tracking: batch/expiry/serial/IMEI capabilities post through the same immutable ledger as ordinary stock (physical units move to the destination warehouse on tracked transfer, duplicate tracked receipt with same serials conflicts as inventory_conflict), tracked transfer preserves cost and invalid receipts roll back consumption, issued identifiers must exist in that tracked warehouse (identifier_not_in_stock), a batch without expiry remains issuable, the server-local-date expiry policy blocks yesterday-expiring lots for manual issue and transfer while a lot expiring today remains issuable/transferable (expired_batch)
scenarios.notes: Mapped by QA Batch 3 (docs/qa/phase-2-coverage.md). Note: expiry is exercised without sleeps via relative lot dates (expiry tomorrow/yesterday/today).

scenarios.title: Posting idempotency and hash protection: identical post replays with the same document id and a changed payload conflicts (operation_key_conflict), the canonical v2: request hash distinguishes delimiter/newline-swapped payloads that collide under the legacy hash (and enforcing the conflict leaves balances and row counts unchanged), and a seeded legacy unversioned OperationKey hash conflicts and does not repost (no extra document rows or movements)
scenarios.notes: Mapped by QA Batch 3 (docs/qa/phase-2-coverage.md).

scenarios.title: Count and reversal hash identity: identical reversal replays with the same document and a changed reason conflicts; the count hash covers cost and physical unit identities, so changing only UnitCost or removing one IMEI from the discovered unit conflicts while counts of 5 stay one document/movement and exactly 1 InventoryPhysicalUnits/3 InventoryIdentifiers rows
scenarios.notes: Mapped by QA Batch 3 (docs/qa/phase-2-coverage.md).

scenarios.notes: Mapped by QA Batch 4A (docs/qa/confirmed-bugs.md CONFIRMED-002, repaired; docs/qa/phase-3-coverage.md updated). The mismatched-payload selector is an xUnit theory that materializes six independent cases (changed_amount / changed_type / changed_date / changed_notes / changed_notes_whitespace / other_customer), each in a fresh disposable GUID SQLite database; the screen flows remain a manual remainder. Replay ownership is decided from stored metadata only (sales provenance columns, CustomerPayments reference equality, RequestHash==OperationKey); no key prefix is reserved — manual keys starting with CP- or sale- replay identically (pinned by Customer_manual_key_starting_with_cp_or_sale_prefix_replays_and_legacy_payment_row_still_conflicts), while a colliding actual customer-payment row is rejected without a false replay. Id here matches the test-file header comment (verified gap previously recorded in docs/qa/phase-3-coverage.md).
